subject: Renewal: uptier rollback window, temporary credit buffer & invoice sync
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@novumretail.com>

Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@novumretail.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal/questions (Oct)

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the draft term sheet. Quick Qs from finance before we loop legal:
- Can you hold current unit rates for Q1 of the renewal even if we exceed this year's commit? We expect a big Black Friday uplift and want to avoid a retro price spike.
- If we commit to a 30% uplift in committed capacity for 12 months, can we get a short ‘rollback window’ (30 days) after go-live to adjust the commit without penalty?
- Our procurement team wants a small bridge credit if usage in month 1 is >120% of the committed ramp.

If helpful, I attached our projected consumption for Nov-Dec.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Grant
VP, Platform & AI
Novum Retail

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@novumretail.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@novumretail.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal/questions (Oct)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. Summarizing so we’re aligned:
1) Temporary rate hold for Q1 post-renewal if you hit the Black Friday uplift -> we can offer a 90-day price shelter that keeps unit rates at current levels for the first billing quarter after renewal.
2) 30-day rollback window on the uplifted commit -> we can provide a 30-day adjustment window but with a small pro-rated true-up if the final commit is materially lower (we propose 10% cap on retro true-up for that window).
3) Bridge credit for month-1 >120% usage -> propose a one-time operational credit equal to 25% of overage charges incurred in month 1, applied to month-2 invoice.

I've attached a draft term sheet with those options (Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf) and a short usage pruning analysis for internal ops. Laura — can you please confirm the 10% cap on true-up is something finance will sign off for a customer of this ARR profile? Ben, please flag any commercial reasons we should adjust the credit %.

Sophie — if that looks directionally right I’ll turn this into a marked-up contract and loop Legal + Procurement.

Thanks,
Elliot Price
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf, Usage_Pruning_Analysis.xlsx

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Novum asks — pricing mechanics and risk

Quick internal note (thread for paper trail):
- Customer wants three things that reduce short-term friction: a Q1 price shelter, 30-day rollback on uplift, and a month-1 bridge credit if usage spikes.
- Proposed commercial math: 90-day shelter; 30-day rollback with 10% max retro true-up; 25% one-time credit on month-1 overage.
- Risk: the 90-day shelter exposes us to sustained overage risk if Novum keeps elevated traffic. Mitigation: require them to keep telemetry hooks on (trace id + token tags) and set a hard burst cap during that 90-day window to avoid runaway spend. Also add a clause that toggles the shelter off if sustained >200% monthly usage for two consecutive weeks.

Laura — can you confirm whether a hard burst cap is enforceable from an ops perspective for Dedicated customers? Ben — will we accept the 25% operational credit? If not, suggest counter (15%?) and highlight margin impact.

Thanks,
Elliot

Thanks for the context, all. I reviewed the proposed mechanics with Finance & Ops:
- 90-day price shelter: approved if we add a burst cap and telemetry SLOs — ops needs the token tags + ingestion metrics to be sent to our ledger. I'll add an SLO requirement in the contract appendix.
- 30-day rollback: Finance is comfortable with a 10% capped retro true-up for that 30-day window, provided the customer signs the amended commit within the first 30 days.
- Month-1 bridge credit: we agree to 20% (not 25%) of overage charges in month 1 applied to month-2 invoice. 20% reduces margin tail risk and is a reasonable concession for onboarding volatility.

Elliot — updated numbers above. Sophie — if you accept 20% we can proceed to legal markup. I've cc'd Ben for commercial concurrence.

Best,

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal/questions (Oct) — revised offer

Sophie — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal review, here's our revised offer to put in the contract: 
1) 90-day price shelter: unit rates held at current levels for first billing quarter post-renewal. Requires telemetry tags and a hard burst cap at 250% of expected month rate during the shelter. Shelter auto-terminates if usage exceeds 200% for 2 consecutive weeks.
2) 30-day rollback window: you may reduce the uplifted commit within 30 days of go-live; retro true-up capped at 10% of the delta between provisioned and final commit. The customer must sign the adjusted commit amendment inside the 30-day window.
3) Month-1 overage bridge credit: one-time 20% credit on overage charges in month 1, applied to month-2 invoice.

If you confirm these three points we’ll prepare a marked-up order form and route to Legal + Procurement for signature. Attached: updated term sheet and a quick Ops checklist for telemetry tags.

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute call with Procurement & Finance to finalize wording?

Cheers,
Elliot
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
